I farm 9 mu, so I do not spread money around carelessly, but I also do not dare cut fertilizer too hard. If wheat or maize loses yield, that hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. I usually start from what I did before and look at what the better fields around me are doing. Here in our place with well water, I will push wheat a bit because wheat needs steady fertilizer and water, and I will not let it go hungry in spring. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the phosphorus into the base fertilizer, give enough nitrogen, and water about 3 times if the season is normal. After wheat harvest, maize comes in tight, so I will keep it simple and fast. I will use hybrid maize seed, mostly no-tillage or very light field preparation, then put on enough nitrogen because maize eats a lot. If rain is short, I will use the well 2 times. For pests and disease, I will spray when I see the problem starting; usually 2 times on wheat and 2 times on maize is what I count on. I will stay close to the way I have farmed before, only using decent seed and not being stingy with fertilizer, because that is the safest way for me to hold yield on 9 mu.
